document_check.note: Xiao S, Li Y, Liu M, Li Y. Electrophysiological evidence of impaired cognitive reappraisal in amnestic mild cognitive impairment: An event-related potential study. Behavioural Brain Research 427 (2022) 113800. It compares 46 aMCI with 47 healthy elderly controls, and HAMD scores are equal between groups (5.26 against 5.28, p = 0.97).

cited_result: MCI showed a smaller reappraisal-related LPP difference (Rea minus Neg) than controls in the later windows (window 2 p = .036, window 3 p = .064, window 4 p = .048), and a smaller reduction in arousal ratings (t = 3.205, p = 0.002), while group HAMD scores were equal (5.26 against 5.28, p = 0.97).
tool_reason: The cited result is a single-session comparison of ERP and behavioural measures between clinic-recruited aMCI and matched community controls, which is a one-time-point group comparison such as MCI against controls.

domains.rationale: Detailed exclusion criteria are given, along with separate aMCI and control inclusion criteria.

signalling.question: Were the criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined?
signalling.quote: Exclusion criteria include: 1) age below 55 years; 2) definite history of stroke; 3) definite history of other diseases of the central nervous system such as infection, demyelinating diseases, and Parkinson’s disease; 4) definite history of mental illness such as schizophrenia, major depressive disorder
signalling.page: 2 (inclusion criteria for aMCI and HECs, p. 3)

domains.domain: 2. Study subjects and setting described in detail
domains.rationale: The recruitment sources for both groups are stated, and demographics and clinical scores are tabulated. Recruitment dates are not given.

signalling.question: Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail?
signalling.quote: Individuals with aMCI were recruited from the Department of Neurology and the Department of Memory Clinic of Shanghai Tongji Hospital. Age-, gender-, and education-matched HECs were recruited from the community.

domains.rationale: Group membership was assigned by a neurologist against stated criteria, and controls had to be normal in all cognitive domains. The memory cut-offs are not specified.

signalling.question: Was the exposure measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: aMCI was designated by a neurologist from the Department of Neurology and the Department of Memory Clinic of Shanghai Tongji Hospital based on the following specific criteria

domains.domain: 4. Objective, standard criteria for the condition
domains.rationale: Published aMCI criteria were used with CDR 0.5 and a neuropsychological battery, although the 'established cut-off' values are not reported.

signalling.question: Were objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition?
signalling.quote: According to the general criteria for aMCI as defined previously [38]
signalling.page: 3 (criterion 3i: "at least two tests within the memory cognitive domain scored below the established cut-off")

domains.rationale: Age, gender, education, depression (HAMD) and anxiety (HAMA) were identified, measured and compared.

signalling.question: Were confounding factors identified?
signalling.quote: Age-, gender-, and education-matched HECs were recruited from the community.

domains.domain: 6. Strategies to deal with confounding stated
domains.rationale: Frequency matching on age, gender and education, plus restriction on HAMD >= 14 and HAMA >= 21. No statistical adjustment.

signalling.question: Were strategies to deal with confounding factors stated?

domains.rationale: A 64-channel EEG recording on an established reappraisal paradigm (Foti and Hajcak), with standard preprocessing. Trial retention was comparable between groups. Blinding of the semi-automatic trial rejection is not reported.

signalling.question: Were the outcomes measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: On average, 22 (72%, confidential interval 69.3%−74.6%) trials remained per condition for the MCI group, and 23 (77%, confidential interval 73.9%−82.1%) trials remained per condition for the HEC group.

domains.rationale: The LPP electrode set was chosen from an exploratory analysis of the same data for 'LPP modulations by Group and Condition factor', and the time windows were set by visual inspection of the grand averages. Group by condition effects were then tested in those same electrodes and windows, a circular selection that inflates false positives. The four window-wise group t-tests were not corrected for multiplicity, and a non-significant window (p = .064) is described as part of a significant 1100 to 5000 ms difference. 26 of 72 aMCI (36%) were excluded after recruitment, 8 of them for 'abnormal behavioural data', and only completers were analysed. One t and p pair is inconsistent (t = -1.170, p = .091).

signalling.question: Was appropriate statistical analysis used?
signalling.quote: we first performed an exploratory analysis of LPP [46–48] to identify the sets of neighbouring electrodes showing LPP modulations by Group and Condition factor.
signalling.page: 4 (windows "based on visual inspection of the grand average waveforms and the results of the LPP exploratory analysis", p. 4; results "second (t = −2.125, p = .036), third (t = −1.874, p = .064) and fourth (t = −2.009, p = .048) time windows", p. 6; "Twenty-six aMCI subjects and three HECs were excluded", p. 2)

overall: High (by this review's JBI rule: item 8, appropriate statistical analysis, is No)
overall_rationale: The design is otherwise adequate, with matched groups, defined criteria and equal HAMD. But the cited late-window LPP result depends on electrodes and windows selected from the same data by group-by-condition effects, has no multiplicity correction across windows, and comes from a completer sample after 36% post-recruitment attrition in the aMCI group.

applicability.rationale: The aMCI group comes from a single Shanghai memory clinic and excludes depressed participants. The 26 of 72 aMCI who could not complete the task or had abnormal behavioural data were excluded, so the results apply to less impaired aMCI.
